summary: The agents roster refresher no longer refolds back to back under a stream of local writes. A claim this node commits now cuts the refresher's 1 s pause only if an agent card reads it. That is decided by the same subject list the roster's incremental fold uses: agent, mission-run, run-generation, step-run, message, exec and pty. Such a claim now ends the pause at the larger of 400 ms and twice the fold, rather than 100 ms and the fold's length, and never later than the full pause: a fold over half a second keeps the full pause, as before. Fresh reads keep their 100 ms floor. In the daily load test, roster publishing had used about 4 times its earlier daemon CPU, because the load's 4.5 local claims a second cut nearly every pause to 100 ms. A person still sees their own write after about 400 ms plus a fold, instead of up to a second.

replay.detail: No claim, fold or projection change; only when the roster refresher folds.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or migrations. One new read of claims by store index and origin.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, registry or coordinated member upgrade change.

compatibility.detail: No API, CLI or wire change. A served roster is as fresh as before, within about 400 ms plus a fold of a local write.

recovery.detail: Reverting restores the 100 ms local cut for every local claim, and its CPU under a stream of local writes.
